transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve noticed I keep getting up when I’m supposed to be sitting with everyone else. Like in staff meetings or even at dinner, I’ll suddenly stand up to refill coffee, check a handout, or walk to the back of the room, even when there isn’t really any urgent reason. It’s not a huge thing, but it’s happening enough that I’m concerned about it.
When you get up like that, do you feel physically restless just beforehand?

Yes, I think so. It’s not always that I notice it right away, but when I’m sitting at my desk grading essays or in church, I’ll catch myself tapping my foot, clicking my pen, or shifting around in the seat. Sometimes I have to tell myself, “Just settle down.”
Do you ever feel driven to get up or move because of a repetitive thought or a ritual you feel you have to do?

No, I don’t think so. It doesn’t feel like I have a thought I have to obey or a ritual I need to complete. It’s more just… I feel antsy or uncomfortable sitting still, and then I get up without thinking much about it.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?
Not especially, no. I worry about the usual things—work, family, money sometimes—but I wouldn’t say I spend a lot of time worrying about lots of different things.
Do you often interrupt other people before they’ve finished speaking?

Yes, I do sometimes. In group discussions, like at book club or curriculum meetings, I’ll jump in before someone has finished because my response is already in my head. I don’t mean to be rude, but it just comes out before I stop myself.
Did you have similar trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Yes, I did. Even when I was little, my report cards would say things like I was bright, but I couldn’t stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother used to joke that before I was ten I’d worn a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener.
Do you often have trouble keeping your attention on a task from start to finish?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I can usually finish things if I know they have to be done, especially at work. I haven’t noticed that as a big problem for me, at least not compared with other things.
Do you often find it hard to wait your turn?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it as a major issue now. I mean, I can get impatient like anyone, but I don’t know that I’d say I often have a hard time waiting my turn.
Do you often blurt out an answer before a question has been completed?

Yes, I do sometimes. In group discussions, like at book club or in curriculum meetings, I’ll jump in before the other person has quite finished. It’s like the answer is already in my head, and I say it before I’ve stopped myself.
Do you often feel driven to do things before thinking them through?

Yes, I think so. Since my youngest left for college and the house is quieter, I notice I don’t really stop much. I’ll go from lesson planning to laundry, then to softball practice, then chopping food for some community event, without really pausing. Even on nights when I’ve told myself I’m going to rest, I end up doing the next thing before I’ve really thought it through.
Do you often lose things you need for work or daily activities, like keys, papers, or your phone?
I’m not sure I’d say often. I misplace things now and then, like anyone, but I haven’t noticed it being a regular problem for work or daily life.
Do you often feel as if you’re “on the go,” as if driven by a motor?

Yes, I do feel that way a lot. Since my youngest left for college and the house got quieter, I notice I’m just constantly moving from one thing to the next—lesson planning, laundry, softball practice, chopping food for some community event. Even when I’ve told myself I’m going to rest for the evening, I usually end up doing something else without much of a pause.
Do these restlessness and impulsive behaviors cause significant problems for you at work, at home, or in relationships?

Yes, somewhat. It’s not ruining things, but it has started to affect my relationships at work and in my community. In meetings or at book club, people seem to lose patience with me, and I can tell I’ve frustrated them. I usually leave feeling embarrassed instead of feeling connected.
Do you often get easily distracted by things going on around you?
I’m not really sure. I can get distracted sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it being a big or frequent problem for me.
Do you often avoid or put off tasks that require sustained mental effort, like paperwork, grading, or long reading?
I don’t think so, not in a way I’ve really noticed. I mean, grading and paperwork aren’t my favorite, but I usually get through them when I need to. I wouldn’t say I’m regularly avoiding them.
Do you often have trouble doing quiet activities, like reading or relaxing, because you feel the need to keep moving or talking?

Yes, that does happen. At book club, or even just a quiet evening with my husband watching a movie, I have trouble just sitting there quietly. I’ll start making comments, or get up and rustle around in the kitchen, or suggest we do something else. It’s like I feel I need to be doing something.
Do you often make careless mistakes or miss details in your work?
I don’t think that’s a major issue for me. I mean, I’ll make the occasional mistake like anyone does, but I haven’t noticed that I’m often missing details or making careless errors in my work.
